Alex —

Appreciate the note and great meeting earlier. I attached a concise term sheet and the sequence-length profile we captured during the demo runs. High-level answers here and a quick proposal below so procurement has something to review:

Summary answers:
- INT8 quantization: typical token-cost reduction of ~40–50% for our mid-sized generation models (4–12B class) with negligible quality regressions on short completions. We recommend INT8 for BrightCloud pilot workloads (enrichment + short-form generation).
- INT4 / extreme quant: gives additional cost savings but increases risk for hallucinations and is recommended only for deterministic embedding/encoder workloads, not completion-heavy paths.
- Commit levels: to trigger a discount on the Optimize toolkit license and deeper onboarding credits, we need a 6-month pilot commit (recommended) or a 12-month commit for the most significant commercial concession.

Pilot proposal (concise):
- 3-month technical pilot (no up-front platform fee) + $30k in platform credits to offset usage as we tune batching/kv-cache.
- If BrightCloud signs a 6-month commit (monthly minimum $40k consumption), we offer a 20% discount on hosted API/Optimize toolkit list prices and an additional $15k onboarding credit.
- 12-month commit (monthly minimum $80k) => 28% discount + $60k one-time migration/onboarding credit and two dedicated performance tuning sessions with our applied ML team.

Technical guardrails / recommended settings for pilot:
- Batching: start with dynamic batching window = 30ms, max batch size = 16. For low-latency endpoints reduce window to 10–15ms and use batch size 8.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for repeated prompt templates; TTL=24h for session-level caching for enrichment pipelines. Expect 15–30% token reductions depending on prompt reuse.
- Quantization: enable INT8 act-order kernels on our Mx series; fall back to FP16 for long-form creative completions > 512 tokens.

Attachments: RDW-Toolkit-TermSheet-v1.pdf (term sheet with pricing tiers) and seq_length_profile_brightcloud.csv (sample seq length distribution).

I copied Karthik for any technical clarifications on kernel/compatibility. If procurement wants an itemized row for "savings per 1M tokens" with both INT8 and batch savings modeled I can add that quickly.

Thanks,
